lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: A photo of an empty yellow office. Seven years later it has its own movie.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: May 12, 2019. On an anonymous paranormal board, someone asks for pictures that "feel off". They post a big, empty, yellow room.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: Another anonymous user writes a short description. If you fall out of reality in the wrong place, you land in the Backrooms. The smell of old carpet. The buzz of lights. Roughly six hundred million square miles of empty rooms.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: Nobody's name is on it. Writers added levels and monsters. A forum grew past 157,000 members by 2022.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: In January 2022, a 16-year-old uploaded a short found-footage video, made in Blender and After Effects over about a month. It grew into a series.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: Where was the photo from? In 2024, fans traced it to a 2002 snapshot on a store renovation blog in Wisconsin. The room is now an RC car track.

lines.speaker: gloom
lines.text: The scariest place on the internet was a furniture store. Gloom: "Aisle three, probably."
